title: Set 78

sentences.ko: 우리 팀에 회의 때는 다 좋다고 해 놓고 한 시간쯤 지나면 다시 생각해 봤다고 메시지 보내는 사람이 있어. 그래서 이번 주에만 같은 슬라이드 세 장을 두 번이나 다시 만들었어. 근데 내가 그 사람을 진짜 좋아한다는 게 짜증나는 부분이야. 못되게 굴기라도 하면 그냥 한마디 하면 되는데.
sentences.text: There's a woman on my team who agrees with everything in the meeting, and then an hour later I get a message saying she's been thinking about it. So we've redone the same three slides twice this week. And I actually like her, which is the annoying part, because if she were a jerk about it I could just say something.

alts.text: So this woman on my team nods along to everything in the meeting, and then an hour later I get a message saying she's been thinking about it. We've redone the same three slides twice this week. And I actually like her, that's the annoying part, cause if she were a jerk about it I could just say something.

There is a woman on my team who agrees with everything during the meeting, and then an hour later I receive a message saying that she has been thinking it over. As a result, we have revised the same three slides twice this week. And I genuinely like her, which is the frustrating part, because if she were unpleasant about it I could simply say something.

sentences.note: **which is the annoying part** 는 앞에 한 말을 받아서 바로 그게 제일 거슬리는 지점이라고 짚는 말이다. **if she were a jerk about it** 의 be a jerk about it 은 어떤 일을 두고 못되게 군다는 뜻이다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 휴대폰 케이스를 시켰는데 자동차 바닥 매트를 보냈더라. 상자 크기가 비슷하지도 않으니까 누가 봐도 제대로 안 보고 보낸 거지. 그래서 반품을 하려는데 앱에서 송장 사진을 올리라는 거야. 근데 송장은 유일하게 제대로 된 건데. 내 이름까지 찍혀 있고. 아무래도 사람한테 직접 전화해야 될 것 같아.
sentences.text: I ordered a phone case and they sent me a floor mat for a car, and the boxes aren't even close to the same size, so somebody really wasn't looking. Then I go to start the return and the app wants a photo of the label, but the label is the one thing they got right, it's got my name on it. I think I'm going to have to call an actual person.

alts.text: So I order a phone case and what shows up is a floor mat for a car, and the boxes aren't even close to the same size, so somebody really wasn't looking. Then I go to start the return and the app wants a photo of the label, but the label's the one thing they got right, it's got my name on it. I'm gonna have to call an actual person, I think.

I ordered a phone case and they sent me a floor mat for a car, and the boxes are not even close to the same size, so someone truly was not paying attention. Then I went to begin the return and the app asked for a photo of the label, but the label is the one thing they got right; it has my name on it. I believe I will have to call an actual person.

sentences.note: **the one thing they got right** 는 다 틀렸는데 그것 하나만 제대로 됐다고 할 때 쓴다. **an actual person** 은 앱이나 자동 응답 말고 진짜 사람을 뜻한다.
sentences.situation: 배달 시켰는데 엉뚱한 게 와서 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 갈비는 네 말이 맞았어. 근데 거기가 그렇게 시끄럽다는 말은 안 했잖아. 60센티쯤 떨어져 앉았는데도 동생한테 계속 다시 말해 달라고 해야 했어. 그래도 또 갈 거야. 금요일만 아니면. 그리고 창가 그 자리 날 때까지 기다릴 거고.
sentences.text: Okay, you were right about the short ribs, but you did not tell me how loud it is in there. We were sitting maybe two feet apart and I still had to keep asking my sister to repeat herself. So I'd go back, just not on a Friday, and I'd hold out for that table by the window.

alts.text: Fine, you win on the short ribs, but you never told me how loud that place is. We were like two feet apart and I still kept asking my sister to say it again. So I'd go back, just not on a Friday, and I'd hold out for that table by the window.

You were correct about the short ribs, but you did not tell me how loud it is in there. We were seated perhaps two feet apart and I still had to keep asking my sister to repeat herself. So I would return, though not on a Friday, and I would wait for that table by the window.

sentences.note: **hold out for** 는 아쉬운 대로 하지 않고 원하는 게 될 때까지 버티며 기다린다는 뜻이다. **you were right about** 는 상대 말이 맞았다고 인정할 때 쓰는 말이다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

sentences.ko: 주말 내내 집 밖으로 한 번도 안 나갔는데 기분이 아주 좋아. 솔직히 나도 좀 놀랐어. 보통은 일요일 오후쯤 되면 주말을 통째로 날렸다고 스스로한테 짜증이 나거든. 근데 이번엔 꼭 가야 할 데가 없었으니까 그냥 소파에서 책 읽고 폰은 배터리 나가게 뒀어. 그게 다야.
sentences.text: I didn't leave the apartment once all weekend and I feel great about it, which honestly surprised me, because usually by Sunday afternoon I'm annoyed at myself for wasting the whole thing. But I didn't have anywhere I had to be, so I just read on the couch and let my phone die. And that was pretty much it.

alts.text: Never left the apartment once all weekend and I feel great about it, which honestly surprised me, cause usually by Sunday afternoon I'm mad at myself for wasting the whole thing. But I didn't have anywhere I had to be, so I just read on the couch and let my phone die. That was pretty much it.

I did not leave the apartment once all weekend and I feel wonderful about it, which honestly surprised me, because ordinarily by Sunday afternoon I am irritated with myself for having wasted the entire weekend. However, I had nowhere I needed to be, so I simply read on the sofa and allowed my phone to die. And that was essentially all.

sentences.note: **let my phone die** 는 충전하지 않고 배터리가 다 나가게 그냥 두는 것이다. **that was pretty much it** 은 별다른 일 없이 그게 사실상 전부였다고 마무리하는 말이다.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 십 분쯤 뒤에 나 좀 거들어 줄래? 집에 가서 개 내보내야 한다고 할 건데 거의 사실이야. 이웃이 여섯 시에 데리고 나갔으니까 벌써 다섯 시간 지났거든. 그냥 피곤하다고 하면 너희 아버지가 한 병 더 따실 거고 그럼 나 새벽 한 시까지 여기 있어야 돼. 그러니까 내가 일어나면 그냥 맞장구만 쳐 줘.
sentences.text: Can you back me up in about ten minutes? I'm going to say I've got to get home and let the dog out, and it's mostly true, my neighbor took him out at six and that was five hours ago. Because if I just say I'm tired, your dad opens another bottle and then I'm here till one. So when I stand up, just nod along.

alts.text: Hey, can you cover for me in like ten minutes? I'm gonna say I've gotta get home and let the dog out, and it's mostly true, my neighbor took him out at six and that was five hours ago. Cause if I just say I'm tired, your dad opens another bottle and then I'm here till one. So when I stand up, just nod along.

Would you be able to back me up in about ten minutes? I intend to say that I need to get home and let the dog out, and it is largely true; my neighbor took him out at six and that was five hours ago. Because if I simply say that I am tired, your father will open another bottle and then I will be here until one. So when I stand up, please nod along.

sentences.note: **back me up** 은 내가 하는 말에 편들어 주고 거들어 준다는 뜻이다. **nod along** 은 따지지 않고 고개 끄덕이며 맞춰 주는 것이다.
sentences.situation: 저녁 모임에서 먼저 일어날 구실 만들기

reviewed: 2번 formal 에서 telephone an actual person 은 요즘 아무도 쓰지 않는 말투라 call an actual person 으로 바꿨습니다. 격식은 말투만 올리는 것이지 옛말을 쓰는 게 아닙니다.
2번 formal 의 the application requested a photograph 도 지나치게 굳어 있어 the app asked for a photo 로 낮췄습니다. 뜻은 그대로입니다.
2번 casual 이 text 와 앞부분이 거의 그대로 겹쳐서(I order a phone case and they send me...) 뒷부분을 what shows up is a floor mat for a car 로 바꿔 말투 차이가 나게 했습니다.
3번 casual 의 We're sitting like two feet apart and I still kept having to ask 는 현재와 과거가 섞여 어색해서 We were like two feet apart and I still kept asking 로 시제를 맞췄습니다.
3번 casual 도 앞부분이 text 와 같아서 Fine, you win on the short ribs, but you never told me how loud that place is 로 고쳐 캐주얼답게 짧게 만들었습니다.
5번 formal 의 Would you be able to support me 는 back me up 의 뜻(내 말에 편들어 달라)이 아니라 막연한 도움이 되어 버려서 back me up 을 그대로 살렸습니다. back me up 은 격식 자리에서도 쓸 수 있는 말입니다.
